triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module encoded superseded text timelessly: its single open-ended versions asserted a $3,000 dependent exemption and $7,400/$3,700/$2,700 personal exemptions for every year from 2003/2013 onward, so it returned pre-2024 law for 2024+ even though HB 1021 raised the dependent exemption to $4,000 for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2024, HB 463 raised it to $5,000 for 2026, and SB 56 (Sections 2-2 through 2-6, applicable to taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2024) replaced the taxpayer/spouse personal exemptions.
triage.triage_notes: Read the cited session laws through the pinned corpus release: HB 1021 (2024) revises 48-7-26(b) to '$3,000.00 $4,000.00 for each dependent' and is 'applicable to all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2024'; HB 463 (2026) revises it to '$4,000.00 $5,000.00 for each dependent'; SB 56 Section 4-1(2) makes Sections 2-2 through 2-6 applicable from TY2024. The fix adds effective_to '2023-12-31' to the three personal-exemption parameters and to the derived personal_exemption_deduction selector (correct: after TY2024 O.C.G.A. 48-7-26(b) contains only the dependent exemption), and adds versions[1] 4000 (2024-2025) and versions[2] 5000 (2026-) to dependent_exemption_amount. It also converts module.source_verification.corpus_citation_path to corpus_citation_paths listing the three acts, which is provenance bookkeeping riding along with the substantive change. Alternative kind: amount_mismatch, since for 2024-2026 the module also returned the wrong dollar amount; I chose wrong_period_or_effective_date because the defect definition explicitly covers 'timeless encoding of superseded text' and the fix's decisive edit is the missing effective_to plus successor versions. Follow-up commit 5474dca0e ('Complete state income tax RuleSpec campaign', same PR) adds SB 56 effective-date excerpts and a deferred_output for 2027+ because HB 463's $125 annual increases are contingent on revenue-condition delay tests. Companion test file gained 24 lines of new-period cases in the same commit.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute the first reader and could not: the parent file gave every rule in 48-7-26 exactly one open-ended version (`effective_from: '2013-01-01'` / `'2003-01-01'`, no `effective_to`), so the module affirmatively asserted $7,400/$3,700/$2,700 personal exemptions and a $3,000 dependent exemption for 2024 and every later year. The cited codified source itself contradicts that — the O.C.G.A. 48-7-26 record resolved through the pinned release carries the note "This version is effective until January 1, 2024. For version effective January 1, 2024, see the following version." — and HB 1021 § 1 replaces subsection (b) wholesale with "a personal exemption in the amount of $3,000.00 $4,000.00 for each dependent", "applicable to all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2024", while HB 463 § 2-2 goes to "$4,000.00 $5,000.00 for each dependent". The fix changes encoded meaning exactly as described: it closes the superseded windows at 2023-12-31 and adds 2024 and 2026 versions, so period/version-window is the operative kind rather than amount_mismatch (no existing value was corrected; each old number was right for its own window) and not mechanical (versions and effective dates are precisely what changed).

triage.verifier_notes:
Evidence read: bundle JSON, diff 000.diff, parent blob 9ff9a7aa:us-ga/statutes/48/48-7-26.yaml (confirmed zero `effective_to` keys pre-fix), and three provisions resolved through corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current (us-ga/statute/48/48-7-26, .../session-laws/2024/hb1021/document-1, .../session-laws/2026/hb463/document-1).

Three secondary points for a reviewer. (1) The commit subject names 48-7A-3 as the headline logic fix, but this is module index 0 of four; its own change is the period repair, so the commit message is not the right evidence anchor here — the diff and the PR bullet "repair Georgia PIT law through 2027, including 2026 standard/dependent amounts" are. (2) Four of the five named rules (joint/separate/other personal exemption amounts and personal_exemption_deduction) receive ONLY `effective_to: '2023-12-31'` with no successor version, which is consistent with HB 1021/SB 56 replacing subsection (b) entirely with a dependent-only exemption; that asymmetry is why amount_mismatch is the weaker kind. (3) Residual gap not part of this defect, worth a separate look: the new 2026 version is open-ended at 5000, but HB 463 § 2-2 continues "provided, however, that such deduction shall be increased by $125.00 annually beginning on January 1, 2027, until such deduction reaches $6,000.00, provided that such increases in such deduction shall be subject to the same delays as those applied to standard" — the PR body describes 2027 deductions as contingent, so the escalator may be deliberately deferred rather than missed.

The diff also carries genuinely mechanical content (module summary rewrite, single `corpus_citation_path` widened to a `corpus_citation_paths` list, added proof atoms). Those alone would be mechanical/provenance, but they are not what carries the verdict; the version-window and new-version edits are.
